questions.stem: Copper conducts electricity well because each of its atoms has
options: loosely held outer electrons that can drift freely
questions.explanation: Free (valence) electrons in metals drift under an applied e.m.f., forming the current.

questions.stem: Which material is used to make the outer covering of house wiring cables because it is a good insulator?
questions.explanation: PVC has very high resistivity and is flexible, so it is used to insulate cables.

questions.explanation: Brown 1, black 0, orange multiplier 1000: 10 x 1000 = 10 kΩ; gold = ±5%.

At a junction, 5 A flows in. Two of the three outgoing branches carry 2 A and 1.5 A. By Kirchhoff's current law the third branch carries
questions.explanation: Current in = current out: 5 = 2 + 1.5 + I, so I = 1.5 A.

questions.explanation: C = 6 x 3/9 = 2 µF; Q = CV = 2 µF x 50 V = 100 µC (same on each in series).

questions.stem: A disadvantage of a digital multimeter compared with an analogue meter is that it
options: needs a battery to work on every range
questions.explanation: Digital meters need a power source and show rapidly changing readings poorly; the other features are advantages.

A two-input gate gives output 0 ONLY when both inputs are 1. The gate is
questions.explanation: NAND is the inverse of AND: output is 0 only when all inputs are 1.

questions.stem: A sinusoidal voltage has a peak value of 100 V. Its r.m.s. value is about
questions.explanation: Vrms = 0.707 x Vpeak = 70.7 V; 63.7 V is the average value.

questions.stem: A series circuit has L = 0.1 H and C = 10 µF. Its resonant frequency is about
A transformer in which the windings are placed on the central limb and surrounded by the core is the
questions.explanation: In shell type the core surrounds the windings; in core type the windings surround the core limbs.

questions.topic: Principles of operation of a transformer
questions.stem: A transformer with a turns ratio of 20 : 1 is fed from 240 V. The secondary voltage is
questions.explanation: Vs = Vp x Ns/Np = 240/20 = 12 V.

questions.topic: Losses and temperature rise in transformers
questions.stem: The transformer loss caused by the resistance of the windings is the
questions.explanation: I²R loss in the windings is copper loss.

questions.stem: A transformer delivers 4 kW while its total losses are 200 W. Its efficiency is about
questions.explanation: η = output/(output + losses) = 4000/4200 = 95.2%.

questions.stem: In the block diagram of a d.c. power supply, the block that smooths the pulsating output of the rectifier is the
questions.explanation: A filter (usually a reservoir capacitor) smooths ripple; the regulator then stabilises the voltage.

questions.stem: Which single-phase motor uses a capacitor in series with its auxiliary winding only while starting?
questions.explanation: In a capacitor-start motor the centrifugal switch disconnects the capacitor and auxiliary winding once up to speed.

questions.explanation: A shunt-wound machine has its field across the armature terminals.

questions.stem: The d.c. motor best suited to a lathe needing nearly constant speed under changing load is the
questions.explanation: Speed of a shunt motor falls only slightly with load.

questions.stem: The Shiroro power station on the Kaduna River generates electricity mainly by
questions.explanation: Shiroro is a hydro-electric station; falling water drives turbines coupled to alternators.

questions.stem: Rectangular PVC or metal channels with removable covers, fixed to walls to carry many cables, are called
questions.explanation: Trunking is an enclosure with a removable lid; conduit is a tube.

questions.stem: Compared with a rewirable fuse, a miniature circuit breaker (MCB) has the advantage that it
options: can be reset after tripping without replacing anything
questions.explanation: An MCB is reset with a switch; a fuse element must be replaced.

questions.stem: Earth loop impedance must be kept low so that, during an earth fault,
options: no current flows in the earth wire
the voltage at the socket rises
enough current flows to operate the protective device quickly
the fault current is limited to 1 mA
questions.explanation: A low loop impedance ensures high fault current, so the fuse or breaker disconnects rapidly.

questions.stem: The test carried out to ensure that switches and fuses are connected in the phase conductor only is the
questions.explanation: A polarity test checks that single-pole devices are in the phase (live) conductor.

questions.stem: Before working on a lighting circuit, an electrician should
options: isolate the supply and lock off the switch
ask someone to hold the live cable
questions.explanation: Safe isolation with lock-off prevents someone re-energising the circuit.

questions.stem: On overhead transmission towers, insulators are used to
options: prevent current flowing from the conductors to the tower
questions.explanation: Porcelain or glass insulators support the conductors while isolating them from the earthed tower.

questions.stem: In a distribution substation, the feeder is
options: a circuit carrying power from the substation to an area
questions.explanation: Feeders carry power from the substation to distribution transformers or load areas.

questions.stem: Cleaning and oiling the bearings of a ceiling fan every six months, before any fault appears, is
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance is planned in advance to stop faults occurring.

questions.topic: Maintenance and repair of electrical appliances
questions.stem: An electric iron gives a mild shock when touched but still heats. The fault is MOST likely
options: a faulty thermostat contact that never closes
an earth fault with a broken earth connection
questions.explanation: The live part touches the metal casing and the earth path is broken, so the casing becomes live.

questions.stem:
(a) State Ohm's law. [2 marks]
(b) A 24 V supply feeds a 4 Ω resistor in series with a parallel combination of 6 Ω and 3 Ω. Calculate (i) the total resistance, (ii) the supply current, (iii) the current in the 6 Ω resistor. [6 marks]
(c) Calculate the power dissipated in the 4 Ω resistor. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) current through a conductor is directly proportional to the p.d. across it provided temperature and physical conditions are constant
2 marks: (b)(i) parallel = 6 x 3/9 = 2 Ω; total = 6 Ω
2 marks: (b)(ii) I = 24/6 = 4 A
2 marks: (b)(iii) p.d. across parallel = 4 x 2 = 8 V; I6 = 8/6 = 1.33 A
2 marks: (c) P = I²R = 16 x 4 = 64 W
questions.explanation: Parallel 6‖3 = 2 Ω, total 6 Ω, I = 4 A. Parallel p.d. 8 V, I in 6 Ω = 1.33 A. P in 4 Ω = 64 W.

questions.stem:
(a) Define capacitance and state its unit. [2 marks]
(b) Capacitors of 4 µF, 6 µF and 12 µF are connected (i) in series, (ii) in parallel. Calculate the equivalent capacitance in each case. [4 marks]
(c) Calculate the energy stored when the parallel combination is charged to 200 V. [2 marks]
(d) State two applications of capacitors. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) ratio of charge to p.d. C = Q/V; farad
2 marks: (b)(i) 1/C = 1/4 + 1/6 + 1/12 = 1/2; C = 2 µF
2 marks: (b)(ii) C = 4 + 6 + 12 = 22 µF
2 marks: (c) E = 1/2 CV² = 0.5 x 22 x 10^-6 x 40 000 = 0.44 J
2 marks: (d) any two: power supply filtering, motor starting, tuning circuits, power factor correction, coupling (1 each)
questions.explanation: Capacitance is Q/V (farad). Series 2 µF; parallel 22 µF. Energy = 0.5 x 22 µF x 200² = 0.44 J. Used in filters, motor starting, tuning.

questions.stem:
(a) With a labelled description, explain the construction of a permanent-magnet moving-coil instrument. [4 marks]
(b) A moving-coil meter has a resistance of 10 Ω and gives full-scale deflection with 15 mA. Calculate the shunt resistance needed to convert it into an ammeter reading up to 1.5 A. [4 marks]
(c) State two disadvantages of the moving-coil instrument. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) permanent magnet with soft iron pole pieces and cylindrical core; light coil on aluminium former pivoted in jewelled bearings; control springs (hairsprings) also carry current; pointer and scale; eddy-current damping (1 each for four features)
1 mark: (b) shunt current = 1.5 - 0.015 = 1.485 A
1 mark: (b) p.d. across meter = 0.015 x 10 = 0.15 V
2 marks: (b) Rs = 0.15/1.485 = 0.101 Ω
2 marks: (c) any two: d.c. only without rectifier, costly/delicate, errors from ageing springs/magnet (1 each)
questions.explanation: Construction: permanent magnet, pole pieces and core, pivoted coil, hairsprings, pointer, damping by aluminium former. Shunt = 0.15/1.485 = 0.101 Ω. Disadvantages: d.c. only, delicate, costly.

questions.stem:
A 5 kVA single-phase transformer has iron loss of 120 W and full-load copper loss of 180 W.
(a) Calculate its efficiency at full load and unity power factor. [4 marks]
(b) Calculate its efficiency at half load, unity power factor. [4 marks]
(c) State two methods of cooling transformers. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) output = 5000 W
1 mark: (a) losses = 120 + 180 = 300 W
2 marks: (a) η = 5000/5300 x 100 = 94.3%
1 mark: (b) output = 2500 W
1 mark: (b) copper loss = 180 x (0.5)² = 45 W; total = 165 W
2 marks: (b) η = 2500/2665 x 100 = 93.8%
2 marks: (c) any two: natural air (AN), oil-immersed natural (ON), oil with forced air (OFAF), forced oil/water (1 each)
questions.explanation: Full load: 5000/(5000 + 300) = 94.3%. Half load: copper loss is quartered to 45 W, so 2500/2665 = 93.8%. Cooling by air, oil natural, forced air or oil.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the two main parts of a three-phase induction motor. [2 marks]
(b) Explain why the rotor of an induction motor can never run at synchronous speed. [3 marks]
(c) A 2-pole, 50 Hz motor runs at 2880 rev/min. Calculate the slip. [3 marks]
(d) Name two methods of starting three-phase induction motors. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) stator and rotor (1 each)
3 marks: (b) at synchronous speed there would be no relative motion between field and rotor, so no e.m.f., no rotor current and no torque; rotor must slip behind
1 mark: (c) Ns = 120f/P = 3000 rev/min
2 marks: (c) slip = (3000 - 2880)/3000 = 0.04 = 4%
2 marks: (d) any two: direct-on-line, star-delta, auto-transformer (1 each)
questions.explanation: Stator and rotor. With no relative motion there is no induced current and no torque. Ns = 3000, slip 4%. Starters: DOL, star-delta, auto-transformer.

questions.stem:
(a) List four tests carried out on a new domestic installation before it is connected to the supply. [4 marks]
(b) Describe how the insulation resistance test is carried out. [4 marks]
(c) State two safety precautions during installation testing. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) continuity of protective conductors/ring, insulation resistance, polarity, earth electrode resistance/earth loop impedance (1 each)
1 mark: (b) isolate supply, remove lamps/disconnect equipment, close switches
1 mark: (b) use insulation resistance tester (megger) at 500 V d.c.
1 mark: (b) test between phase and neutral, and between each conductor and earth
1 mark: (b) reading should be not less than about 1 MΩ (regulation minimum)
2 marks: (c) any two: ensure supply is off and locked, warn occupants, use correct instrument range, discharge cables after test (1 each)
questions.explanation: Tests: continuity, insulation resistance, polarity, earth. Insulation test with a 500 V megger between conductors and to earth, expecting at least about 1 MΩ. Isolate, warn others and discharge after testing.
